thread.title: Himax Should Get Bought Out At This Price - Himax Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ:HIMX)

author: Chris Lau
title: Himax Should Get Bought Out At This Price - Himax Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ:HIMX)
text:
When shares of Himax Technologies ( HIMX ) hit rock bottom earlier this week and traded at an intraday low of $3.03, the deep undervaluation, relative to the promised growth ahead, signals it's time that the company get bought out. Going private is another option. The main reason is that the company is preoccupied with pivoting its business toward growth. Publicly, the stock is subject to manipulation and the problem for Himax is that its efforts in defending the value are better spent on other activities.
If Himax privatizes, what's the company worth? At its current market cap of under $600 million, the market is assigning no value to the growing areas of the business. Instead, it's discounting the lack of progress for 3D sensing, developed in partnership with Qualcomm ( QCOM ). Certainly, the slowdown in smartphone sales, signaled by Apple ( AAPL ) suppliers cutting output and lowering revenue forecast, is a negative for Himax. That Himax has a leading 3D sensing solution is of no value when phone makers are scaling back on their ambitions. Himax touts its superior 3D sensing covering all three types of technologies: Structured light, active stereo (“ASC”) and time-of-flight.
Headwind in 3D Sensing Lumentum ( LITE ), which cut its outlook and sent the stock from $55 down to $37, had reported revenue growth of 154% year-on-year, driven by demand for its 3D sensing. It completed its acquisition of Oclaro after China’s approval, and forecast a production ramp into its second quarter. Despite a slow uptake for Himax’s solution, high-end Android smartphone suppliers will still need to eventually include an all-encompassing solution. In 2019, 5G-supported devices will encourage consumers to upgrade. Device makers will have to add a richer feature set for customers to justify a device upgrade.
To date, Himax has only one customer ready to employ the technology for mass production. That's simply not enough. And after the company shifted its R&D expenses and capex in this segment, investors are punishing the company by selling the stock. Executive Dr. Biing-Seng Wu said he would invest $5 million personally in HIMX stock . With his current 20.7% ownership, the chairman could take it a step further and find partners to take the company private.
Since markets are assigning no premium to Himax’s future growth catalysts ahead, the company could take the company private at these levels. At a forward P/E of 18 times and EPS growth of 25% over the next five years, insiders should not have a problem attracting bidders.
Near-term risk in 3D sensing Himax stumbled in the third quarter when customers held back on ordering the 3D hardware. High prices plus the extra time needed to integrate the technology into smartphones hurt initial sales. Yet when Apple is charging more than $1,200 for devices and Samsung is doing the same, other smartphone suppliers have room to absorb the higher hardware costs. If it does not do so, it risks losing market share to those two leaders.
Himax may re-purpose the technology to target the security and surveillance market with success. Ambarella ( AMBA ) marketed its computer vision technology enough to report good enough revenue levels. Ambarella’s results ended up squeezing shorts, sending the stock from as low as $30 before the earnings report to around $43. And for Himax, which already forecast stronger sequential revenue growth, stronger 3D sensing sales, WLO revenue, vision sensor technology in CMOS and LCoS in the augmented reality space may all restore investor confidence.
CES 2019 At CES 2018, the hype in 3D and augmented reality pushed HIMX stock to $11. But at 66% below that level, anyone speculating on the stock could make another play on Himax. Any news where Himax announces design wins during CES 2019 will justify a stock rebound back to the forward 30 times P/E range, or $5 - $7 a share.

Your takeaway The P/E compression is expected as stock markets fall and risk aversion goes up. Of course, this justifies HIMX stock trading at these levels. I'm not ready yet to abandon the view that the company may potentially ramp up sales in 3D sensing. Using a five-year DCF growth exit model, assume a discount rate of 10-12% and steady revenue growth of 5% in that period.
